items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: Now, these bands today, I don't play with anybody now, except Godfrey once in a while.

ctx.x: I don't play on the phone. No, I call him pretty regular. Uh, I-
Now, these bands today, I don't play with anybody now, except Godfrey once in a while. You don't play with me that much. I don't want no fucking-
I don't want no frassling jobs.

items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-10-02
items.q: He was playing drums with us, yeah. When Crum would take off a night now and then, Godfrey would play for us.

ctx.x: You know which club he's talking about, Dick? Curly's?

Curly's. Curly's Corner. He, uh, whatever. He, uh, he went in there and the first night we were in there, but you know how loud Jumbo blew. He told Jumbo, he says, for Christ's sake you're playing so loud I can't even think. So, uh, Jumbo says, Sarah, he says, I got a contract with this guy. He says, you gotta pay me. He says, he can't find me. He says, after all I quit WWL and everything else. So, here comes two ladies down in the bar over there and some guy's wife, I don't know who it was, D'Antoni went over…

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: Doc died. Three bass players that worked with me the past 10 years.

ctx.x: Did Stranicos ever go over to the Gulf Coast? He was from the Gulf Coast.

Ellis was from the Gulf Coast. Yeah. It was Stranicos' man that we used to play over there with Charlie Wagner, Johnny Roniger, Meyer Weinberg, Doc Benitez. You know, he died recently. Oh, yes, he did, yeah. Doc died. Three bass players that worked with me the past 10 years. All died in a very short period of time.
Yes, sir. Who was the ottoman?
